root_cause_criterion.criterion: At `X86_get_insn_id()`, the `find_insn(...)` result must satisfy `i != -1` so the function writes `insn->id` before `printOperand()` later reads `MI->flat_insn->id` inside the immediate-printing switch.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable witness decodes the alternate immediate-move opcode whose generated `insns[]` table row is missing in the vulnerable tree. `find_insn(...)` therefore misses, the guarded `insn->id` assignment is skipped, and the fixed table restores the missing mapping so the same protected sink executes only after `insn->id` has been written.
root_cause_criterion.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace reaches `print_operand_sink` with `x86_id_lookup.lookup_hit=0`; the fixed trace reaches the same sink with `x86_id_lookup.lookup_hit=1`.

nodes.description: At the source-level MSan sink, `printOperand()` reads the 4-byte public instruction id in `switch(MI->flat_insn->id)` while the vulnerable run still has fewer initialized bytes than the switch consumes.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable trace records `print_operand_sink.flat_id_read_bytes` greater than `print_operand_sink.flat_id_initialized_prefix_len` at the immediate-printing switch.

nodes.description: Immediately after the guarded write site, the vulnerable run still has fewer initialized bytes than `sizeof(insn->id)` because the only public-id assignment was skipped on the crashing path.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable trace records `x86_id_lookup.public_id_initialized_prefix_len` smaller than `x86_id_lookup.public_id_size` at the end of `X86_get_insn_id()`.

edges.relation: The same public instruction-id storage whose guarded write is skipped at `X86_get_insn_id()` is later re-read through `MI->flat_insn->id` at the immediate-printing sink.
